title: A track that feeds another track drops its input until TrackManager wires the link
body:
A `Track` subscribes to its input device in its own constructor, but a track whose output is another track only gets output receivers later, when `TrackManager` wires the inter-track connections. Input arriving in that window is dropped without being processed.

`Track`'s constructor builds the pipeline and immediately subscribes to the input device:

```scala
private val pipeline: MidiSerialProcessor = MidiSerialProcessor(
  Seq(tuningChangeProcessor, tunerProcessor).flatten, outputDeviceHandle.map(_.receiver).toSeq)

inputDeviceHandle.foreach(_.transmitter.addReceiver(receiver))
```

`outputDeviceHandle` is populated by a `collect` that only matches `DeviceTrackOutputSpec`, so for a `ToTrackOutputSpec` track the pipeline starts with **no** output receivers. `TrackManager.replaceAllTracks` constructs every track first and only then runs its "Wire inter-track connections" loop, so between those two points the track is live on its input device with an empty transmitter — and `MidiProcessorReceiver.send` drops a message without calling `process` when the transmitter has no receivers.

Consequences in that window: notes are dropped rather than tuned, tuning-change triggers (e.g. a pedal) are not seen by `TuningChangeProcessor`, and `MidiChannelStateTracker` misses the messages it needs to track held notes and controller state — so a note already held when the link is wired is unknown to the tuner afterwards.

Before #281 the pipeline always had `Track`'s own output `MidiSplitter` as a receiver, so `process` ran and the tuner and tracker observed the stream even with nothing connected downstream. #281 removed that splitter (design decision D6), which is what exposed this.

The window is short — the remaining tracks' construction — so this is unlikely to bite in practice unless a device is already streaming while the composition loads. Possible directions:

- Subscribe to the input device after the inter-track wiring, rather than in the `Track` constructor, so a track never receives before it can forward.
- Or have `TrackManager` construct all tracks, wire the links, and only then start the inputs, making the ordering explicit rather than incidental.

Related: `#297` covers the same "dropped without processing" behaviour for `Track.initMidiMessages`.

Found while reviewing #289.
